customer: So I've got this full-size SUV I'm thinking of trading in because honestly the family keeps growing and I want something even bigger, and over the years I put a lift kit on it and a pretty loud exhaust, plus there's a really nice custom stereo my brother-in-law installed. I figured all that stuff would bump up what you'd offer me, but my neighbor said it might actually hurt? Anyway, what's the deal with modifications, and should I do anything with the stereo before I bring it in here in Virginia?
agent: Your neighbor's right, unfortunately. Aftermarket modifications rarely add value, and things like lift kits and loud exhausts usually lower the offer because we may need to return the car to factory condition. If you'd like to keep the custom stereo, please remove it before the appraisal. If any modification does change your offer, the specialist will show you why, and our article "What can change your offer" has more details.
